info.bio: Everclear es una banda de rock formada en Portland, Oregón, EE.UU. en 1992. Durante casi toda su existencia consistió en Art Alexakis en las voces, Craig Montoya al bajo y Greg Eklund a la batería. Eklund sustituyó al primer batería, Scott Cuthberg, en 1994. Montoya y Eklund dejaron la banda en 2003 pero Alexakis ha continuado actuando como Everclear con una nueva formación.

scenes.name: Grunge
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El grunge, revival del hard rock de los setenta y renacimiento musical de Seattle, fue uno de los grandes fenómenos de los noventa (casi solo en EE UU). Green River lo inauguran (Come On Down) y Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Melvins y Mudhoney fijan sus cuatro puntos cardinales; Nirvana, con Nevermind, lo convierten en una tragaperras y en la banda sonora de la crisis nerviosa de una generación. Después, Alice In Chains (Dirt), Foo Fighters, Hammerbox, GodHeadSilo, Everclear, Stone Temple Pilots, Tool (el grupo más innovador de la segunda generación: Aenima, Lateralus), God Machine, Helmet, Quicksand, Urge Overkill, los Smashing Pumpkins (Siamese Dream, Mellon Collie), Scarce, Creed, Bush, Manic Street Preachers, Silverchair.

podcast.title: Boston Mosh Pit Lawsuit (1997)
podcast.body: During Everclear's performance at The Paradise club in Boston on November 13, 1997, three members of the New England Patriots – quarterback Drew Bledsoe, backup quarterback Scott Zolak, and offensive lineman Max Lane (who weighed 305 pounds) – were in the mosh pit. Max Lane arced off the stage and landed on 23-year-old Tamika Messier, crushing her and causing severe neck, shoulder, and arm injuries, including two herniated discs and three fused vertebrae. Messier filed a $1.2 million lawsuit on December 10, 1997, against the club, Lane, Bledsoe, and Everclear, which was settled in March 1999, with Everclear contributing to the settlement and subsequently facing higher liability insurance premiums. "Everclear abandoned ended up with higher insurance premiums because of an NFL lineman."

podcast.title: Lawsuit and Settlement (1997-1999)
podcast.body: Following the stage-diving incident, Tamika Messier filed a lawsuit on December 10, 1997, against The Paradise club, Max Lane, Drew Bledsoe, and Everclear, seeking damages. The case concluded in March 1999 with a $1.2 million settlement, primarily covered by Lane and Bledsoe, but Everclear also contributed, significantly increasing their liability insurance premiums. podcast.title: MS Diagnosis (April 2017)
podcast.body: Art Alexakis began noticing symptoms in 2015, including stumbling and forgetting lyrics, which some mistook for drinking or drug use. He dismissed it as tiredness. After a car crash in April 2017 and a subsequent arm twinge, an MRI, arranged by his daughter, revealed lacerations on his brain indicative of multiple sclerosis. He kept the diagnosis quiet for four years. "Then in April 2017, he was on his way to pick up his daughter at school. It was raining, and he crashed into a jeep. Now nobody was hurt, but then two weeks later, he had a twinge in his arm that he thought was left over from a snowboarding crash or maybe the jeep crash. His daughter set him up with an MRI, and that's when he learned the news. They found lacerations on Art's brain indicative of multiple sclerosis."

podcast.title: Managing Multiple Sclerosis
podcast.body: Initially viewing his MS diagnosis as a death sentence, Art Alexakis's prognosis improved after working with doctors who prescribed Copazone. He takes three injections a week, avoids inflammatory foods like sugar, and has been told by his doctor he could have another 30 years if his condition remains stable. While he can no longer run and has taken up swimming, his guitar playing remains unaffected, and he doesn't expect to be confined to a wheelchair. "The prognosis isn't as bad as he thought it might be, and Art realizes that he may need a cane later in life, but he shouldn't be confined to a wheelchair. He hopes. He gives himself three injections a week, yes to stay away from inflammatory foods like sugar, and if things continue the way they are, Art's doctor says he could have another 30 years."

podcast.title: Stage Diving Injury Lawsuit
podcast.body: On November 13, 1997, during an Everclear show at The Paradise in Boston, stage diving was prevalent. Two New England Patriots players, Drew Bledsoe and Scott Zolak, along with lineman Max Lane (who weighed 305 pounds), climbed onto the stage. Lane dove into the crowd, landing on 23-year-old Tamika Messier and crushing her. She suffered neck, shoulder, and arm injuries, including two herniated discs and three fused vertebrae. Messier filed a lawsuit on December 10 against the players, their club, and the band, eventually receiving $1.2 million for her pain and suffering. "Lane Dove. He landed on 23 year old Tamika Messier crushing her. She suffered injuries to her neck, shoulders and arms."

xref.title: Multiple Sclerosis Diagnosis
xref.body: In 2017, Art Alexakis, the leader of Everclear, was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS), a disease that targets the central nervous system by attacking the protective coating around nerve fibers. This condition can lead to a range of issues, including problems with walking, vision, and chronic fatigue. "In 2017, he was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, a disease of the central nervous system."
